sections.title: 1. WHAT THIS IS
rows: A complete content architecture to make <domain> the most authoritative site in <category>, in <languages>.
The whole: service pages, industry pages, author pages, a <n>-term glossary, and more.

sections.title: 2. ARGUMENT
rows: Demand is tiny and expensive (or: where the demand is)
Three measured examples with volume and CPC from this run.
Own several hundred qualified long-tail terms and be the source answer engines quote. State AI Overview presence found on the commercial queries checked.
What the site audit and SERP pulls showed about competitors: who holds page one, what they cannot do.
Traffic looks disappointing for three to six months. Keyword coverage, citation share and conversions are the metrics that matter.

sections.title: 3. RESEARCH
rows: Every pillar is anchored to something the client sells, qualified by the industry it sells into.
The fastest-rising topics in the map with measured percentages.
High-volume terms rejected with the audience reason; note where a rejected term is used only as a glossary entry.
Pulled per market for <markets>, in the local language and in English where relevant.
Every core keyword classified with a confidence score; below 60 percent the page serves both readings.
Checked directly; where measured intent and the result page disagree, the result page wins.
Pulled per page (or per head term where deferred) and folded into the H2 outlines.

sections.title: 4. COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE
rows: Identified from the live result pages and the domain audit.
Who they are and why they cannot occupy the client's angle.

sections.title: 5. SITE ARCHITECTURE
rows: All editorial, organised into pillar directories.
The definitional layer answer engines quote.
Company page plus one author page per named specialist.
Count of existing URLs by status: enhance, merge, redirect, unchanged.
301 every legacy URL to its directory-style path and keep the map permanently.
Problem-led pages sit inside the topic pillars so every pillar ends in a conversion page.

sections.title: 6. LANGUAGE PLAN
rows: Which, which is primary, which were considered and not built and why (with measured evidence).
Subdirectories on one domain; slug policy; regional hreflang annotations.
All pages (or the subset) — translation via DeepL with the locked glossary; automated keyword-presence check.

sections.title: 7. PREPARATION WEEK 0
rows: Publish on the current site or a new one; URL structure fixed now; legacy URLs 301-redirected.
Connect the domain to the Snoika system at DNS/CDN level and verify paths resolve before the first page is written.
Lock the per-page measured native keywords and the terms that stay English.
Approve page template, author boxes, answer-block position, FAQ schema and hreflang setup.
Name the reviewer, confirm the three-working-day review service level, agree what approved means.

sections.title: 8. WEEKLY PUBLISHING CYCLE FROM WEEK 1
rows: This week's pod is drafted, edited by Snoika and sent for review.
Client review, three working days; edits made within the window; English approved.
Hreflang built for the set; publication in every language in scope at once; Friday link pass.
Month 1: <n>/week skeleton; month 2: <n>/week cluster hubs and first demand pages; months 3-4: <n>/week; month 5 onward: <n>/week.
Total months to publish all pages at the cadence; deadline-driven pages pulled forward.

sections.title: 9. INTERNAL LINKING AND PUBLISHING PODS
rows: Every pillar hub links down to every cluster hub and page in its pillar.
Every cluster hub links to every page in its cluster.
Every page links up to its cluster hub and pillar hub within the first two screens.
Every page links horizontally to 3-5 siblings and 1-2 pages in another pillar.
Every informational page links to at least one service or industry page.
First use of a defined term on any page links to its glossary entry.
Every page links to its author page, and the author page links back to the article list.
Nothing deeper than three clicks from the homepage; pillar hubs reach 15-30 inbound links as the pillar fills.
A page in one language links only to pages in that language.
Pages ship in weekly groups so every internal link works on the day it goes live; no page links to a URL that does not exist yet; Friday link pass connects live pages to the new ones.

sections.title: 10. MEASUREMENT AND REPORTING
rows: Monthly: keyword coverage (top-20 per market), citation share (AI Overviews and answer engines), conversions (calls booked and enquiries as analytics events, attributed to page and pillar), traffic as context.
Baseline in week 0; first movement expected on the demand pillar within three months, on the category terms within six.
